request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have dates, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How holds behave now**
- Each person row has **Hold from** and **to** fields and a **Hold** button. A blank from-date means the sheet's today; a blank to-date means the hold has no end. A person can build up several holds, and each one is listed in the row (`person-hold-line`).
- A hold whose to-date is before its from-date is refused with an error in the row. Nothing is saved and nothing is written to the audit file.
- **On hold** shows yes if the person has any hold at all, whatever its dates.
- **Totals:** an open claim is left out only if it is dated within one of the person's holds and no statement has bound it. A claim bound by a statement always counts. The server, the screen and the statement step all use this same rule.
- **Audit:** holding writes `PERSON_HELD … name=<name> from=<date>`. The audit file no longer gets `PERSON_RELEASED` lines. There is no release action any more: a hold ends on its to-date.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V32__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table and drops the old `held` column. Anyone already on hold gets one hold with no start or end date, so their totals stay as they were.

**Choices you may want to change** (the request didn't settle these):
- "Open" still means OPEN or PENDING, as it did before, so a PENDING claim inside a hold is left out too.
- When a new statement is taken, open claims dated within a hold are not bound, which carries over the old rule. So re-taking a statement can take a previously bound claim inside a hold out of the totals.
- The endpoint moved from `POST …/hold` to `POST …/holds`, and it now takes `{from, to}`.

The main changes are in `PersonService.hold`, `Rollup.heldOut`, the new `PersonHold` entity, and `core/people.ts`, `core/claims.ts` and `features/people/people.ts` on the front end.
